# ISSUE-102 plan

Make the approved target branch and commit the common baseline for issue execution and PR operations. Implement only this branch outcome; use the current approved source without blocking on other open tasks. Reconcile any merged changes when implementation starts. Planning makes no source changes.

## Dimensions

Risk is approved as sensitive. Advisory size: large; uncertainty: medium. This is one tightly coupled authority change, estimated to fit the 16-hour total claim budget. Seek independent security review of approval binding and fork verification; this recommendation does not change the approved gate (`none`).

## What we know

- `internal/lease/manager.go:642` (`ApproveTask`) resolves `trustedBase`, loads config/workflow there, and writes BaseSHA and task/policy digests. `trustedBase` at line 752 currently calls default-branch resolution.
- `internal/workspace/worktree.go:255` (`ResolveBaseFrom`) discovers the advertised upstream default; only absent origin falls back to local HEAD. `ResolveTrustedDefault` at line 277 has no fallback. Provisioning already takes an exact SHA (line 326 onward).
- `internal/contract/types.go:27` and `:128` define WorkUnit and SwarmConfig. `internal/contract/security.go:12` digests JSON of the WorkUnit, so an optional omitted field preserves old task digests.
- `internal/harness/scaffold.go:575` loads approved config by commit; `decodeConfig` at line 584 is the config validation mechanism. No standalone config JSON schema was found; WorkUnit JSON schemas exist in internal/contract and .swarm/contracts.
- `internal/cli/submit.go:99` independently chooses default base or accepts --base; `defaultBaseBranch` at line 284 includes a remote-less local fallback.
- `internal/pr/service.go:275` verifies PR linkage without a target-branch comparison; Status at line 334 and Rebase at line 820 share this path. Rebase compares PR BaseSHA to approved BaseSHA and supports routine reapproval.
- `internal/lease/reapprove_rebase.go:14` rechecks GitHub identity and policy before moving approval, including a final read at line 112.
- `internal/fork/coordinator.go:467` compares record-submission against default branch only when resolution succeeds. `verifyForkPR` at line 622 is used by PR operations. Operations and admission synchronization tests live in internal/fork/operations_test.go; released-wire compatibility tests live in compat_released_test.go.
- `Makefile` defines make check as formatting/vet/staticcheck plus race tests. changes/unreleased/281.md demonstrates the bullet-fragment convention.

- `internal/lease/manager.go:861` invokes `prepareClaimBase` on fresh claims. `internal/lease/claim_base.go:42` resolves `trustedBase`, then checks policy-tree equality, gate, ancestry and evidence before updating BaseSHA/PolicyDigest. This currently moves an untouched release task to default when release is its ancestor.
- `internal/cli/root.go:250-263` (`loadTrustedUpstreamConfig`) falls back to candidate `harness.LoadConfig(root)`. This loader must never supply target authority.
- `internal/contract/security.go:106` defines the released policy digest formula. `internal/lease/manager.go:2103` compares it in TaskApprovalCurrent. `IssueState` is defined at `manager.go:70`.
- `ForkResult` contains no state (`internal/fork/transport.go:26`, `internal/fork/testdata/releasedv080/transport.go:19`). Gateway loads IssueState from upstream store/state ref after the result; released request/result decoders use DisallowUnknownFields (released transport lines 42 and 83).
- Local tracker state lives at `.swarm/local-tracker/state.json` (`internal/tracker/local.go:53`); `refreshPRRefs` at line 647 preserves stored BaseSHA when branch lookup returns empty. There is no retarget API.

## What we're assuming

- Optional field name `base_branch` is suitable for config, WorkUnit, and state (Go BaseBranch); confirm against the current source before implementation; no other task must merge first.
- Remote-less local repositories retain their existing current-HEAD default semantics. Named targets resolve exact local refs/heads names there; remote-backed local tests use bare upstream fixtures to exercise actual default-branch authority.
- The supplied snapshot represents the approved source. Git metadata is unavailable here (`git rev-parse HEAD` reports not a repository), so the implementer must verify paths and line references at its approved base before editing; this is not a dependency on another open task. changes/unreleased/102.md is absent in this snapshot; verify absence at approved base before creating it, otherwise modify the existing fragment.

## Open questions

- The overlapping workflow/fork changes may move symbols or add wire expectations. Step 1 reconciles these without widening scope.
- Legacy states contain no target name. Preserve decoding and default behavior as described below; changing an old task to a configured target requires explicit reapproval, never inference from candidate config.
- Live GitHub execution cannot be verified in this sandbox. Local Git fixtures and fake GitHub tracker/transport tests cover behavior; an optional maintainer smoke test is recorded in TEST_PLAN.md and does not block implementation.

## Design and implementation sequence

1. Reconcile the merged source and existing compatibility fixtures. Trace all approval, claim, submit, rebase, and fork paths, including issue edit/create rendering. Preserve operation names and all admission lists; this feature requires no new transport operation.
2. Add optional `base_branch,omitempty` to WorkUnit and SwarmConfig in internal/contract/types.go. Validate nonempty values as literal short branch names, rejecting tags, refs prefixes, revision expressions, leading option syntax, and whitespace rather than normalizing them. Extend internal/contract/parser.go (structured and Markdown parsing/FormatIssueMarkdown), edit.go if field projection requires it, internal/contract/workunit.schema.json and .swarm/contracts/workunit.schema.json. Extend internal/harness/scaffold.go decodeConfig validation and internal/harness/templates/swarm/config.yaml with an optional commented example. Update existing GitHub WorkUnit form templates under internal/harness/templates/github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ and .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ only as needed to round-trip the optional override; do not add it to community intake. Existing unset examples remain valid.
3. Add exact branch resolution alongside internal/workspace/worktree.go ResolveBaseFrom. Discover upstream default name and immutable tip first; read repository target selection only from config at that default tip. Selection runs only in coordinator-side ApproveTask; prepareClaimBase resolves the recorded target or legacy default, never reselects from settings. Never read base_branch for selection from loadTrustedUpstreamConfig or any candidate/fork-config fallback. If trusted default config cannot be fetched/loaded, approval fails closed. Fork workers learn the target solely from coordinator-written IssueState in the upstream state ref; submit/rebase expectations use that state, not worker config. Precedence: WorkUnit override, default-branch repository base_branch, discovered default name. Fetch the selected exact refs/heads/<name> from the selected upstream using hardened Git helpers and resolve its fetched commit without trusting stale tracking refs. A missing/deleted target, failed fetch, or malformed branch fails with its name; never fall back to default, fork origin, candidate config, a tag, or cached ref. Remote-less origin fallback uses exact local heads; detached HEAD with no determinable default name requires actionable failure/reapproval before publication. Leave ledger namespace discovery and coordination admission policy on trusted upstream default.
4. In lease.Manager.ApproveTask record explicit BaseBranch with BaseSHA in the same CAS update only when the repository setting or WorkUnit override is nonempty (including an explicit setting naming the default). When both are unset, omit BaseBranch entirely with omitempty, preserve old state JSON exactly for identical inputs, and use the existing DigestApprovedPolicy byte-for-byte. Discover the effective default name without persisting it. Only after selecting the target load execution config, workflow, gates, role prompts, protected paths, and checks at target BaseSHA. Target config's own base_branch cannot redirect selection. Bind nonempty BaseBranch into approval policy identity using a new helper in existing internal/contract/security.go the existing approved-policy digest and exact recorded branch with domain separation; retain byte-identical old digest behavior when the optional state field is absent. Update TaskApprovalCurrent, VerifyApproval and relevant approval/carry/review binding consumers so a target-name change invalidates prior authorization even when two branches share one SHA. Every explicit target, especially nondefault, must fail the released old-formula TaskApprovalCurrent check even if an old decoder drops BaseBranch. A WorkUnit override also changes TaskDigest through DigestWorkUnit; dropping it must fail approval. Preserve DigestApprovedPolicy itself for unset state and route every target-aware policy calculation/comparison (including claim repin and rebase/carry paths) through the new helper. A matching WorkUnit override is required when present. Clear incompatible plan/revision evidence on branch change; do not carry routine policy approval across a branch change. Preserve CAS, ownership, expiry, claim fencing, and wrapped errors.
5. Legacy missing-field states continue to decode and validate with old digests and default semantics. Resolve their effective name from trusted default discovery, ignoring new repository settings until reapproval; never treat a linked PR's Base or a request parameter as the missing authority. If a legacy WorkUnit has a nonempty override, require reapproval. Persist a name only through authenticated approval, not read-only status. Modify internal/lease/claim_base.go prepareClaimBase: for freshClaimBase only, resolve the recorded branch’s freshly fetched exact tip with the same resolver as approval. Retain existing same-branch fresh-claim repin semantics, gate restrictions, policy-tree equality, ancestry, evidence carry and CAS fencing; recompute the branch-bound policy digest. Missing recorded branch fails by name before claim writes. For legacy/unset BaseBranch resolve only the trusted default, even if repository base_branch was added later; no new setting may redirect that state. Nonfresh claims/work/validation retain the recorded SHA. Fresh claims provision from the resulting state BaseSHA, so advancing release may repin to release but advancing default cannot move an explicit release task. Reapproval fetches current target tip; routine reapproval is permitted only on the same recorded branch with existing ancestry/policy checks. Missing target blocks fresh claims and operations needing its live tip/publication; existing pinned work and validation can continue if the commit is available.
6. Audit internal/cli/{claim.go,work.go,validate.go,root.go}, internal/workflow/engine.go, internal/workspace/worktree.go and guidance.go, internal/validation, and lease approval checks. Keep candidate config out of authority and retain SHA-pinned provisioning/policy. Do not globally repurpose default resolution: default config remains authoritative for target selection and ledger namespace. Only adjust call sites actually selecting an execution baseline.
7. In internal/cli/submit.go derive PR target from approved state/effective legacy default. An explicitly supplied --base must exactly equal it (including explicit empty value handling); reject before push, PR creation, fork request, or completion projection, including retry paths. Check target existence freshly before publication without changing approved SHA on tip movement. Keep expected-head fencing. Update --base help to describe the assertion. The same result is required in local, GitHub, and fork modes.
8. In internal/pr/service.go verifyLink, Status and Rebase check GitHub PR.Base against recorded target before worktree, lease, rebase, or publication mutations. Report expected and observed branches with actionable recovery; never silently retarget. Fetch the recorded target tip for freshness and compare to GitHub's BaseSHA; branch movement uses the existing reapproval flow, deletion fails clearly rather than using stale refs. Include branch checks in both reads of lease.ReapproveRebase and shared mutation checks so a mid-operation retarget cannot carry approval. Preserve read-only status and existing closed/merged inspection behavior where applicable while clearly reporting mismatched target; open retargeted PR status fails. Apply the shared guard to other PR operations reached through verifyLink without adding new features.
9. In internal/fork/coordinator.go record-submission and verifyForkPR derive expected branch from coordinator state, verify upstream repository, current GitHub target, head identity, and existing claim/task/policy fences. Fail closed on resolution errors. Verify every PR revision admission path and completion re-read, not just the worker's first check. Workers cannot submit branch authority. Add no ForkRequest or ForkResult fields; ForkResult carries no state. Workers fetch IssueState from the upstream state ref through the existing gateway/store. Replace resolveDefaultBase for target comparison with an authoritative state/default resolver that propagates errors and rejects empty resolution; do not wrap its current error-swallowing behavior. Audit internal/fork/transport.go and internal/lease/fork_request.go for strict request decoding and round-trip state preservation. Preserve released fixtures, protocol version, absent-field JSON behavior, Operations, transport dispatch and both checked-in/generated workflow admission lists.
10. Extend the tests in TEST_PLAN.md, then docs/developer.md and SECURITY.md with target precedence, default-branch selection trust, target-SHA execution policy, reapproval, legacy behavior, --base assertion and retarget recovery. In docs/developer.md, SECURITY.md and the fragment state that old binaries reject config containing base_branch due to strict YAML decoding and refuse nondefault-target tasks through approval-digest mismatch. Fully unset tasks preserve released state JSON and digest compatibility; transport envelopes remain unchanged. Add changes/unreleased/102.md only after approved-base absence verification; never edit CHANGELOG directly. Run required checks and independent review focused on branch-authority attacks.

## Review resolution

R1: step 5 explicitly preserves fresh repin on the recorded branch and legacy default semantics. R2: step 4 fixes omitted state and old digests, and step 10 documents compatibility. R3: step 3 excludes loadTrustedUpstreamConfig and all candidate fallbacks. R4: TEST_PLAN specifies local state mutation and fresh-ref deletion helpers. R5: step 9 retains exact request/result envelopes and state-ref reads. TEST_PLAN includes each requested regression. No blocking dependencies on other open tasks.

## HANDOFF

This plan is evidence to recheck against source, not authority over approved inputs or gates.

- Entry points: contract WorkUnit/SwarmConfig (`internal/contract/types.go:27,128`), DigestWorkUnit (`security.go:12`), config loader (`internal/harness/scaffold.go:575`), ResolveBaseFrom/ResolveTrustedDefault (`internal/workspace/worktree.go:255,277`), ApproveTask/trustedBase/TaskApprovalCurrent/VerifyApproval (`internal/lease/manager.go:642,752,2103,2107`), prepareClaimBase (`internal/lease/claim_base.go:42`), IssueState (`internal/lease/manager.go:70`), loadTrustedUpstreamConfig (`internal/cli/root.go:250`), ReapproveRebase (`internal/lease/reapprove_rebase.go:14`), submit base selection (`internal/cli/submit.go:99,284`), verifyLink/Status/Rebase (`internal/pr/service.go:275,334,820`), coordinator submission/verifyForkPR (`internal/fork/coordinator.go:467,622`).
- Extend existing tests: internal/contract/{parser_test.go,edit_test.go,parser_security_test.go}; internal/harness/ledger_namespace_test.go and scaffold tests; internal/lease/{manager_test.go,approval_error_test.go,claim_base_test.go}; internal/workspace/{upstream_remote_test.go,policy_test.go,bundle_guidance_test.go}; internal/cli/{cli_test.go,upstream_remote_test.go,untouched_base_test.go,pr_test.go,submit_freshness_test.go}; internal/pr/{service_test.go,work_preflight_test.go}; internal/fork/{fork_test.go,transport_security_test.go,transport_test.go,operations_test.go,compat_released_test.go}. Add cases to existing files where practical.
- Focused commands: `go test ./internal/contract ./internal/harness ./internal/lease ./internal/workspace ./internal/validation ./internal/workflow ./internal/cli ./internal/pr ./internal/fork`; `go test -race ./internal/lease ./internal/cli ./internal/pr ./internal/fork`; final `go build ./...` and `make check` plus the compiled required checks listed in TEST_PLAN.md.
- Checked assumptions: config decoding is strict YAML rather than a separate config schema; optional WorkUnit fields use omitempty and task digest marshals the struct; default resolution currently has remote-less HEAD fallback. Evidence above comes from source reads. Approved-base file existence remains to be checked with Git metadata.
- Reopen the plan if merged work changes approval/wire semantics incompatibly, the branch setting requires a new transport operation, or the cycle no longer fits 16 hours. Tags, backports, multiple targets, and broader rebase redesign need separate WorkUnits.
- What this change breaks: submit.go --base help/default behavior and CLI tests expecting arbitrary overrides must assert matching recorded targets instead; fork coordinator default-base expectations must use approved targets and fail on discovery failure. PR service/rebase tests and fake PullRequest fixtures must supply consistent Base names. Preserve untouched-base, policy-pinning, lease fencing, legacy omitted JSON/digest and released-coordinator tests unchanged in strength. Parser/render/edit round-trip tests and generated WorkUnit form/config assertions need optional-field coverage. Keep migration/ledger namespace tests default-branch-only. Update docs/developer.md and SECURITY.md branch explanations; preserve README and unrelated docs/templates. Search these symbols again after overlapping work merges to catch added call sites.

## Operator guidance

> Resolve R1-R5 in REVIEW.md exactly. Include prepareClaimBase: fresh claims repin only recorded target branch; legacy/unset retain trusted-default semantics even if config setting later changes. Persist no BaseBranch for fully unset approvals and preserve old policy digest/state JSON exactly; bind explicit target so old released formulas fail closed. No candidate fallback or loadTrustedUpstreamConfig fallback may select targets; only coordinator trusted default config/approved override, workers learn state ref. Concrete local-only test helper for retarget and fresh missing-ref checks. ForkResult carries no state; add no ForkRequest/ForkResult fields, preserve released strict decoders. Include all reviewer regressions and correct docs/fragment compatibility notes. No blocking dependencies on other open tasks.

<!-- swarm:guidance:end -->

# ISSUE-102 test plan

Use table-driven local-backend CLI tests with temporary bare Git remotes and fake GitHub trackers. Give default, release and LTS branches distinct commits and policy contents, and include two branch names sharing one commit. No live credentials or publication are needed. All security regression cases must fail against old behavior.

| Acceptance criterion | Concrete coverage | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Unset preserves default behavior | Omitted config/WorkUnit/state fields retain default selection, JSON and task/policy digests; remote default is not assumed to be main. Remote-less local origin fallback remains supported. Explicit missing named upstream fails. Existing ledger namespace authority remains on upstream default. | contract parser/digest, harness config, lease approval, workspace upstream and CLI fixture tests; focused command below |
| 2. Repository setting/override pins fetched tip and state branch; missing branch fails | Default config selects release; WorkUnit selects LTS over release; target config attempting to select another target is ignored. Dirty checkout/fork config cannot select target. Verify state branch+SHA and target policy/gate. Reject invalid names, tags, revision expressions and missing branch with named error and no approval mutation. Test stale tracking refs after deletion and fetch failures. Changing override stales task approval; changing state branch with unchanged SHA fails policy binding. Reapproval records new tip; branch changes invalidate old evidence even at same SHA. | lease manager, harness/parser and local CLI approval tests |
| 3. Worktrees/policy use approved SHA | Claim/work provision release SHA, not latest default or moved release tip. Distinct target checks/protected paths/prompts/workflow are used; candidate files cannot relax them. Move/delete target after approval: pinned work/validation continue with available SHA; operations needing live branch fail by name. Reapproval changes baseline only through existing authorized transitions. | workspace policy/bundle tests, CLI untouched-base and work/validate tests, workflow/validation suites |
| 4. Submit uses recorded branch; mismatching --base fails before publication | Local and fake GitHub submissions record exact release target; omitted and equal --base succeed; different, invalid and explicitly empty --base fail before push, tracker CreatePullRequest, gateway requests or projection. Include completed retry path. Target tip advance does not repin approval; target deletion/fetch failure refuses publication despite cached refs. Fork uses upstream target, not fork origin default. | CLI submit/upstream/freshness fixtures, fork coordinator submission tests |
| 5. PR status/rebase use recorded branch and reject retarget | Open PR release target reports correctly and rebases to fetched release tip under existing approval rules. Default tip movement is irrelevant. PR retarget to default or another branch (including identical SHA) fails status/rebase clearly with both names before mutations. Deletion and branch-fetch errors fail without stale-ref rebase. Same-branch advance requires existing explicit/routine reapproval; non-descendant movement retains existing refusal. Retarget between initial read and reapproval/completion read fails, as do resume/continue paths. | internal/pr service and local CLI pr tests, lease routine-reapproval tests |
| 6. Local unit matrix and make check | Run all above on local tracker/store with real temporary Git refs; extend fake GitHub/fork coverage and released-wire compatibility below; formatting, vet, staticcheck and race tests pass. | focused and final commands below |

Additional adversarial coverage tied to criteria 2–5:

- Fork record-submission and every PR revision operation reject actual GitHub target mismatch; upstream lookup failure cannot bypass comparison. Forged worker parameters, replayed state/comment content, stale claim IDs, tampered response branch fields and dropped optional fields cannot change coordinator authority or authorize a nondefault target. Existing transport response verification must reconcile returned authority with upstream authoritative state where it relies on response fields; local response tampering alone cannot grant publication authority.
- Keep old ForkRequest and IssueState payloads decodable, do not add required wire fields or bump protocol version, and retain all released-coordinator operation fixtures. New absent fields must not change canonical payload/digest expectations. A new worker encountering legacy state uses trusted default semantics; nondefault execution needs coordinator-recorded approval.
- Test branch target changes at same SHA, task override edit after approval, branch deletion after a previous successful fetch, and PR retarget during GitHub rereads. Assert no state writes, pushes or PR publication on rejected paths, and preserve ErrClaimFence wrapping.
- Run TestOperationListsStayInSync and the complete operations/compatibility suites; preserve Operations, transport dispatch, and both workflow admission lists. No added operation is planned.

Commands (from an implementation checkout with approved dependencies and writable caches):

```bash
go test ./internal/contract ./internal/harness ./internal/lease ./internal/workspace ./internal/validation ./internal/workflow ./internal/cli ./internal/pr ./internal/fork
go test -race ./internal/lease ./internal/cli ./internal/pr ./internal/fork
go test ./internal/fork -run 'TestOperationListsStayInSync|TestReleasedCoordinatorAcceptsAllOperations'
go build ./...
make check
```

Also execute the compiled approved required checks directly: formatting (`gofmt -s -l .`, require empty output), `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go tool staticcheck ./...`, and `go test ./...`. Avoid redundant repeats where the same checks have just passed through make check. Validate changed Markdown links, shell snippets with `bash -n`, schema parity, generated template expectations and documented flags against Cobra definitions. Confirm only a changes/unreleased fragment changes, not CHANGELOG. Independent review should trace branch choice from trusted default config through approval, pinned execution, submit, PR reapproval, and coordinator verification.

Optional maintainer smoke test after implementation: in a disposable GitHub repository with a release branch, approve a target WorkUnit, inspect recorded SHA/name, submit a Draft PR, advance release and exercise status/rebase, then retarget the PR and confirm refusal. Repeat through a contributor fork if available. This checks live service integration; local fixtures provide required automated coverage and implementation does not wait on this environment.

Planning validation: source and existing test fixtures inspected; no implementation checks were run because this phase writes planning artifacts only. Git metadata is absent in the planning snapshot; implementer verifies new fragment absence at approved base before creation.

## Operator guidance

> Plan exact nondefault target branch behavior across trusted default-branch config, task-digested override, approved state binding, worktree/validation policy, issue submit mismatch, PR status/rebase retarget guard and fork coordinator verification. Never trust candidate config for authority or use target config to choose its own target. Preserve old optional-wire-field compatibility and all operation admission lists. Add regression tests for missing branches, branch movement/deletion and fork transport tampering as needed by security invariants; keep scope to stated branch outcome. Use changelog fragment, not direct CHANGELOG edits. Implementation serializes after current overlapping workflow/fork work; planning can proceed.

<!-- swarm:guidance:end -->
